analysis.lean: No side or total play: the market is fair against our numbers, and Boston's back-to-back and the 12.5-point spread cancel out.
why: Rating-based home margin is +12.0 (+12.4 blended) against a -12.5 line, which gives a cover probability of about 0.50.
Boston's opponent-adjusted net is +4.9 per 100 against Brooklyn's -6.5. Brooklyn allows an eFG of 0.607 and has been beaten by 26, 4 and 7.
Boston's matchup expected points per shot is 1.174 against Brooklyn's 0.999 (league 1.084), which supports a Boston win but is already priced into the line.
The projected total of 221.9 is almost the same as 222.5. Pace is 103.7 for BKN and 101.3 for BOS, and the samples are only 3 games each.
risks: Boston is on a back-to-back, and a 12.5-point favorite may lose starter minutes in a blowout, which makes a backdoor cover more likely.
Derrick White (right hip) is listed Day-To-Day with a 70% chance to play. His absence is already counted in the projection at -0.7 points.
Every team rating rests on 3 games, so they are heavily shrunk and noisy.
matchups: BOS defense allows centers +17% on threes and forwards +10% on threes (from the measured data). That is a mild tailwind for Brooklyn's perimeter bigs, but the samples are tiny.
Brooklyn takes 45% of its shots from three and Boston allows 50% of opponent shots from three, so three-point variance is high for both teams.
verify: Derrick White's final status before tip.
Whether the spread and total move from -12.5 and 222.5.
Referee crew, which is not posted yet.

judgment.why: Our projection (+12.0, 221.9) and the blend (+12.4, 222.4) sit almost on the market's -12.5 and 222.5, so there is no edge beyond the market's fair price.

analysis.lean: No side or total edge: the line is fair at NYK -4.0 and 219.5, and I'd only play props where the role is clear.
why: Ratings project NYK -0.5 before adjustments. Duren being out moves that to about +3.2 once blended with the market, close to the -4.0 line, so there is no edge.
DET is 3-0 with a +5.7 adjusted net but only 3 games, and NYK is 0-3 at +1.1 adjusted. Both samples are tiny and shrunk, so the raw 118.3 vs 101.7 scoring gap says little.

NYK's offense is shooting a poor 0.476 eFG with a shot-quality matchup of 1.04 points/shot against DET (league 1.084). That favors a lower-scoring game, but the total of 219.5 already sits near our 219.4.
DET's rim-heavy shot mix (37%) meets an NYK defense that allows 30% at the rim, which is average. NYK allows 46% of shots from three (league 42%), which suits Robinson's volume.
Paces are 103.7 and 101.9 against a projected 101.4, so neither side pushes the total.
risks: Ausar Thompson (ankle, full shootaround participant) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are both questionable. The prop model assumes Thompson is out, so DET props could shift if he plays.
With 3 games each, a hot DET shooting start (0.563 eFG) or a cold NYK one (0.476) could easily revert.
matchups: DET's measured defense vs centers (-15% points) comes from games with Duren playing. With him out it likely overstates how hard Towns's night is.
NYK allows +11% threes to forwards, which helps Robinson and Collins on volume (small sample).
verify: Final status of Ausar Thompson and Isaiah Joe near tip.
Whether Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges play their usual minutes, since Alvarado is out.
That the total and spread haven't moved from 219.5 and -4.0 (the total was up +1 earlier).

why: Blended projection is LAL +2.0 and 233.0 against the market's -2.0 and 233.5, so there is no gap worth an adjustment.
The market fair price is home wins 0.539 and 0.50 on both the cover and the over. The line also moved 1 point toward POR and the total dropped 3.
POR's raw numbers (126.0 scored, 101.5 allowed) include a 124-83 win over PHX, and LAL's (128.0 scored, 115.0 allowed) are over only 3 games. Opponent-adjusted nets are close, POR +3.6 and LAL +3.3.
LAL shoots 0.638 eFG but allows 0.526 eFG, and its actual shot value (1.149 per shot) is well above expected (1.078). That kind of shooting usually regresses.
POR has had 3 days off against LAL's 1, but the projection already counts schedule spots (+0.2 margin), so I do not move it again.
risks: Scoot Henderson (20 min) is questionable with ankle soreness. His absence is small, and the market likely prices it.

matchups: POR gives up more to centers (points +9%, threes +22%), which helps Walker Kessler's scoring.
LAL allows only 40% of shots from three and POR takes 50% of its shots from three, so POR's shot mix is facing a defense that gives up fewer threes than the league average.
Thybulle faces his former team (from memory), which is not a reason to change his numbers.
verify: Check that Doncic, Reaves and Kessler have no late injury tags.
Check the referee crew when it is posted.
Re-check the spread and total for movement, since both have already moved.

lessons: Early sample (25 graded picks). Treat every rating as tentative.
Points props are 10-3 with cushion and role signals, but 13 picks is too few to trust. Keep them as normal plays and don't scale them up yet.
Assists, rebounds and threes are 2-10 combined, and rebounds and threes are 0-3 each. Too small to be a rule; lean skip on thin-signal ones.
Picks with no signal are 1-6 and beat the close by -1.6%. Lean skip when no cushion, role, matchup or pace signal backs the pick.
The model said 57.2% overall and 63.5% on 8-12% edges, which went 2-6. Be wary of large edges; don't scale up on size alone.
